_comment_encoding: 12.3-inch NQ5 (Spartan-7 scan). Output is dimmer2048 (binary, 0x000-0x800), not the dimmer800 (BCD 0-800) the file name says: the Spartan-7 bitstream multiplies register 0x35 as plain binary, so BCD gave a staircase (same fix as the 14.6-inch configs, 2ab724d). The file keeps its name because micropanel links it by name. sweep_table calibrations/dimmer800_12_3_nq5.csv was measured through the binary path on 2026-10-14 (FPGA v0x5A, dynamic local dimming OFF = the fixed neutral profile: the nits of full white also depend on the profile boost).

local_dimming_profiles._comment: Day/night local dimming (pixelpipe-fpga docs/dynamic-local-dimming.md; 12.3-inch NQ5 from FPGA v0x59). The detected zone selects raw FPGA 0x1E page-0 registers: ld_alpha 0x31 (LD max/avg blend, 16 = baked default; higher = small content brighter, more halo), pc_tune 0x33 (pixel-compensation gain/64, 64 = 1.0x; from FPGA v0x5D the 12.3 powers up in physical PC mode 0x4C=1, where 64 restores the LD-off luminance of greys exactly and outdoor 83 lifts them ~30 % more for daylight), bl_boost 0x49 (low-APL boost on the LED gain, 64 = off, 90 = up to 2x GD), led_gain 0x43, bl_rise 0x4A. A zone must hold min_dwell_sec before its profile is used; registers then ramp by transition_steps per 500 ms iteration (0 = at once: from FPGA v0x58 the FPGA glides boost and alpha itself; pc_tune still ramps here). static_profile is used when the user switches dynamic LD off (set_ld_dynamic). Night: no extra brightness for dark content. Outdoor: maximum readability. 12.3-inch NQ5: bl_boost stays 64 (off) in every zone (review v4 N17): with the FPGA power-up cap at the LD-off white word (0x7F80) the cap never binds on LD-on content, so a boost would raise everything incl. full white (+18 / +35 %), make the nits table (swept at boost 64) wrong per profile and add power without a rating. Profiles differ in alpha (small content +42 % at 128) and PC only; full white is profile-independent. Enable the boost together with the 14.6 recipe (cap from the rating, LD-on gain to the cap) once the panel rating is known.

thermal_compensation._comment: Only the temperature source is used here (no factor table): the thermal_limit below reads the backlight temperature from the display IOC (0x66, register 0x1002, int16 x 0.1 C).

thermal_limit._comment: Keeps the backlight at about start_c (proportional): limit = 100 - gain_percent_per_c x (T - start_c), floor min_percent, moved by at most step_percent per 10 s reading (1 %: each step is a 1 % brightness change; 1 % deadband on the target); T = mean of the last two plausible readings. LD boost off while T >= start_c, back below start_c - hysteresis_c. No reading = no limiting. Soak values are from the 14.6-inch direct (2026-10-14: ~58 C at the cap, tau ~15 min); not yet measured on the 12.3-inch. start_c is the owner's choice pending the panel's derating spec; choose it as (panel limit - expected residual): the closed loop settles (T_unlimited - start_c)/1.72 above start_c, the 50 % floor removes only ~4.5 C (review v3 §4). 12.3-inch NQ5 (review v4 N20): this IOC NTC rises only ~3 C at full backlight power (LD-off white, tau ~1.5 min + slow drift; 38 -> 41 C in a 22 C room), so it follows the board more than the LEDs; at 60 C the limiter only acts in a very hot environment. Set start_c from the panel rating / sensor placement.
